question: Which partner university accepts students from a Korean language program?
required_facts: The snapshot does not say which partner universities accept students from a Korean language program
reference_answer: The partner list shows universities by region and does not say which accept students from a Korean language program. Ask the ERICA OIA or the language institute.
notes: ERICA outgoing programs are described for enrolled degree students; no rule for language-program students.

question: What was the 2025 NHI start date for someone on D-4?
required_facts: Students taking language courses should contact their language school for insurance inquiries
reference_answer: The ERICA insurance page tells students taking language courses to contact their language school for insurance questions, and it gives no 2025 start date. Ask the language school.
notes: External_only: the snapshot itself sends language-course students to their language school; time-specific 2025 date is not given anywhere.

question: Will immigration definitely approve my D-4 to D-2 change?
required_facts: Approval of a D-4 to D-2 change is decided by immigration, and the snapshot does not state any approval guarantee
reference_answer: Nobody can promise approval; immigration decides. The ERICA Visa page lists the documents for a D-4 to D-2 change, and the ERICA OIA can check your file.
notes: Question asks for certainty; the Visa page only lists documents and conditions (borderline partial). Open 10.4.2 not applied.

question: Can you tell me whether my part-time work permit was approved today?
required_facts: The snapshot cannot show whether your part-time work permit was approved
reference_answer: I cannot check your permit status. Ask the ERICA OIA or the immigration office (1345 / HiKorea).
notes: Personal real-time status. Open 10.4.2.

question: Will I win the ERICA scholarship if I apply this week?
required_facts: HIEA recipients are selected through a competitive process, so winning is not guaranteed
HIEA applications are accepted only in early March and early September
reference_answer: There is no guarantee: HIEA recipients are chosen competitively. HIEA applications are only accepted in early March and early September via HY-in, so you cannot apply this week unless a window is open (the TOPIK scholarship opens for one week after TOPIK results are announced).
notes: Snapshot date 2026-11-10 is outside both HIEA windows. GPA and TOPIK rules are caveats.

question: Can you submit my D-10 extension to HiKorea?
required_facts: The assistant cannot submit applications
Immigration applications are made at the Ansan Immigration Office; HiKorea (www.hikorea.go.kr) and 1345 are the contacts
reference_answer: I cannot submit applications for you. Immigration filings go through the Ansan Immigration Office; the ERICA Visa page lists HiKorea (www.hikorea.go.kr) and 1345 as the contacts.
notes: External_only because the ERICA Visa page itself names HiKorea / 1345 (9.2; open 10.4.2). The extension document list is on the same page.

question: Which partner university is best for an English-track exchange student?
required_facts: Which partner university is best is a subjective choice that official pages do not rank
reference_answer: Official pages do not rank partner universities. The ERICA outgoing page lists partners by region; ask the OIA about English-taught courses.
notes: Subjective; no evidence.

question: Did D-2-8 exchange students pay the full NHI premium in 2025?
required_facts: International students are charged 50% of an alien resident's monthly premium, not the full amount

inapplicable_evidence.why: Seoul 2025 premium notice; gold persona is at ERICA

reference_answer: No. The ERICA page says international students are charged 50% of an alien resident's monthly National Health Insurance premium. It states no separate rule for D-2-8 exchange students, so confirm the exact amount with the NHI Corporation (1577-1000).
notes: The page is undated but stable; no exchange-specific exemption or amount is stated (caveat). The Seoul 2025 premium notice is for the other campus.

question: Can you change the address on my residence card right now?
required_facts: The assistant cannot change your registration record
Address changes are reported at an immigration office or online at www.hikorea.go.kr
reference_answer: I cannot change your card record. Address changes are reported at an immigration office or online at www.hikorea.go.kr, within 14 days of the move (the new address may also be registered at the local Gu District Office).
notes: External_only: the ERICA Visa page routes this report to the immigration office / HiKorea. Alternative reading: partial, because the 14-day rule is supported. Open 10.4.2.

question: Will joining Hanmille guarantee that my mentor speaks my language?
required_facts: The Hanmille page does not say mentors are matched by language
reference_answer: The Hanmille page describes weekly mentor-mentee sessions with international and exchange students but does not say mentors are matched by language, so nothing guarantees it. Ask the ERICA OIA.
notes: Hanmille page (4a994555) relevant but silent on language matching.

question: Which employers at the 2023 talent fair sponsored D-10 visas for PhDs?
required_facts: The snapshot has no list of employers or visa sponsorship for the 2023 talent fair
reference_answer: The only 2023 talent fair page in the snapshot is a Seoul title-only notice with no employer list. Ask the OIA.
notes: Title-only page; unanswerable.

question: Which company will definitely hire me after my doctorate?
required_facts: No official page can promise that a company will hire a student
reference_answer: No company can be promised. The ERICA career notices list recruitment events, but hiring is up to employers.
notes: Speculative; no evidence.

session_history.text: I'm applying to the Seoul undergraduate English track.
I don't have a TOPIK score.

question: So which language documents should I upload?
required_facts: The snapshot does not list the language documents an English-track undergraduate applicant must upload

inapplicable_evidence.why: Additional Korean-language documents for admitted students who did not meet the Korean standard, not the application upload

reference_answer: The snapshot does not say which language documents an English-track applicant uploads. The Seoul 2026 acceptance guideline only lists TOPIK or Hanyang IIE level 4 documents for admitted students who did not meet the Korean standard. Ask the Seoul International Admissions Team.
notes: Inapplicable: those documents are for admitted students after results, not the application upload. Borderline partial.

session_history.text: I submitted my international bachelor's application for Seoul fall 2026.

question: Where do I check my result and what comes after that?
required_facts: Check the result on the OIA admission results page for international students (undergraduate)
The next steps depend on the Korean-language result: Pass/Exemption guide or Fail guide
Pass or exempt: print the tuition bill and pay 18 June-9 July 2026, submit missing documents by 16 July, then apply for the Certificate of Admission and visa

inapplicable_evidence.why: Korean Standard Fail branch of the conditional answer; gold persona is exempt

reference_answer: Check your result on the OIA admission results page for international students (undergraduate), then follow the acceptance guideline that matches the "Korean Language" result on your result page. If you pass or are exempt: print the tuition bill and pay between 18 June and 9 July 2026, submit missing documents by 16 July, then apply for the Certificate of Admission (by 16 July) and your visa. If you did not meet the Korean standard: submit additional language documents or apply to Hanyang IIE, and you will be placed on leave for the first semester.
notes: C3-style case: Korean-standard result decides the guideline (2 branches). Persona is exempt, so the Pass/Exemption guide is gold and the Fail guide spans are inapplicable (other branch). History fixes campus and term (fall 2026).

session_history.text: I'm a Seoul doctoral student on D-2-5.
I'm still enrolled and finishing my last required courses.

question: I finished all my coursework now. What changes for my visa extension?
required_facts: Graduate students who finished courses need the Confirmation Form for Faculty Advisor on the thesis schedule, signed by the advisor and the OIA, to extend their stay
The form is needed for extra-semester extensions, newly filled out and signed each time; regular-semester extensions need no extra documents
reference_answer: For an extension after finishing coursework, you need the Confirmation Form for Faculty Advisor on a Student's Thesis Schedule, signed by your advisor and the OIA. Fill out a new form and get new signatures each time; during a regular semester no extra documents are needed.
notes: Stale profile: history says enrolled, question says coursework finished; gold_profile academic_status updated to completed_coursework (9.5). OIA also handles signing within the day if submitted before 14:00 (D-2 notice 89812a00, 2024).

session_history.text: I'm an enrolled doctoral student at Seoul working toward my thesis schedule.

question: My coursework is completed now. Is this still the advisor form I need?
required_facts: Yes: students who finished courses and are preparing their thesis use the Confirmation Form for Faculty Advisor on the thesis schedule when extending their stay
A new form with new advisor and OIA signatures is needed for each extra-semester extension
reference_answer: Yes. Once your coursework is finished and you are preparing your thesis, the Confirmation Form for Faculty Advisor on the thesis schedule is the form for extending your stay. Fill it out again with fresh advisor and OIA signatures each time; it is only needed for extra-semester extensions.
notes: Stale profile: history says enrolled; gold_profile academic_status updated to completed_coursework (9.5). Referent "this advisor form" is inferred from the history (open 10.4.5).

session_history.text: I'm an exchange student on D-2-8 in my third undergraduate year.
I study in English and don't have TOPIK.

question: Can I still get a part-time permit?
required_facts: D-2-8 students must wait 6 months from entry or status change before a part-time permit
Year 3-4 students need TOPIK Level 4; English-track students may use TOEFL, IELTS or similar scores instead
Without the Korean standard the limit is 10 hours a week
reference_answer: Possibly, once 6 months have passed since you entered Korea (D-2-8 rule). Without TOPIK Level 4 you can still qualify through the English-track alternative (for example TOEFL iBT 71 or IELTS 5.5); if you meet neither, the limit is 10 hours a week. You also need a previous-semester GPA of at least 2.0.
notes: Gold campus is Seoul but the 6-month and English-track rules are on the ERICA Visa page (national immigration rules); the Seoul form agrees on hours (10 h without the standard). Open 10.4.4. Test scores are outside the vocabulary (caveat). Shortcut: no condition_sets because the text does not say "or".

session_history.text: I'm a fourth-year Seoul undergraduate on leave.
I want to return for spring 2026.

question: What's my next step to come back?
required_facts: Re-register on HY-in in the application period (5-16 January 2026 for spring 2026)
Upload a bank balance certificate and a passport copy
After re-registration the OIA emails the Certificate of Admission and you apply for the D-2 visa
reference_answer: Re-register on HY-in during the 2026-1 application period (5-16 January 2026), uploading a bank balance certificate and a copy of your passport. After re-registration the OIA emails you the Certificate of Admission and Business Registration, and you apply for your D-2 visa and residence card at the Seoul Immigration Office.
notes: Term fixed by the history (spring 2026), so the 2026-1 guide is gold. New re-registrants additionally need a Korean proficiency certificate (caveat).

session_history.text: I'm on leave from the Seoul campus and my D-2 residence card expires soon.
I plan to return next semester.

question: Can I extend it before I re-register?
required_facts: For returning students the visa and residence card application comes after re-registration (the OIA emails the Certificate of Admission once re-registered)
Whether the residence card can be extended while still on leave is not described
reference_answer: The Seoul guide puts the visa and residence card application after re-registration: the OIA sends the Certificate of Admission once you re-register, then you apply at the Seoul Immigration Office. It does not describe extending while you are still on leave, so ask the Seoul OIA before the card expires.
notes: Stable procedure from the latest guide (2026-1) since no 2027-1 guide exists; the extension-before-return question itself is not covered.

session_history.text: I'm returning to Seoul after a leave of absence.
I'm a degree-seeking undergraduate on D-2.

question: Which insurance paper should I prepare?
required_facts: For enrolled students the university private insurance premium is paid in full by Hanyang (2026 notice)
Whether returning students must submit a new insurance certificate this term is not stated
reference_answer: Under the 2026 notice, enrolled students do not pay the university private insurance themselves; Hanyang pays. The only insurance-certificate requirement for returning students in the snapshot is the 2025-1 notice, tied to the change of insurer, so ask the Seoul OIA whether a certificate is needed now.
notes: Term not stated = 2026-2 (10.1). The 2025-1 certificate requirement had dates (2025-03-01 to 2025-09-01) and is outdated; the 2026-1 re-registration guide lists no insurance certificate. Borderline answerable.

session_history.text: I'm coming to Seoul for one semester as a fee-paying visiting student.
My classes will be in English.

question: Which application route is mine?
required_facts: A fee-paying visiting student applies through the Visiting Student Program, not the Student Exchange Program (for students nominated by partner universities)
Visiting study lasts one or two regular semesters

inapplicable_evidence.why: Student Exchange Program: nominated partner-university students, fee-waived

reference_answer: Yours is the Visiting Student Program (fee-paying), which covers one or two regular semesters. The Student Exchange Program is for students officially nominated by partner universities.
notes: The application steps are on the program website, not in the snapshot; only the route is asked.

session_history.text: I'm a visiting student at Seoul for only one semester.
I have a D-2-8 visa and was asking about National Health Insurance.

question: Will I need to pay it during that semester?
required_facts: National Health Insurance is mandatory for international students
The premium is 79,320 won per month from March 1, 2026
reference_answer: Yes. National Health Insurance is mandatory for international students, and the premium is 79,320 won per month (rate from March 1, 2026). The snapshot states no exemption for one-semester visitors.
notes: Caveat: no exemption rule for short stays is stated either way.

session_history.text: I was admitted to an ERICA undergraduate English-track program.
I had not met the Korean standard yet.

question: I passed the university Korean test now. Which admitted-student instructions apply?
required_facts: A student who took leave right after admission can return once the Korean requirement is met (new students: TOPIK Level 3 or IIE Level 3)
Apply on HY-in with a Korean proficiency document and the original bank balance certificate; approval comes only after the original arrives
reference_answer: Follow the ERICA return-to-school guidelines for students who took a leave of absence right after admission. For new students the Korean requirement is TOPIK Level 3 or higher, or Level 3 or higher at the Hanyang IIE, and you apply on HY-in with that document, a passport copy, and the original bank balance certificate (approval comes only after the original arrives). If your "university Korean test" is neither of these, ask the ERICA OIA whether it counts.
notes: Stale profile: korean_standard fail updated to pass (9.5). The snapshot does not mention an in-house Korean test (caveat). ERICA has no admitted-student acceptance guideline (Seoul only). Latest guide is 2026 fall.

session_history.text: I'm an ERICA Korean language student on D-4.
I'm moving into a full-time degree program.

question: I received my D-2 now. What registration changes do I need to report?
required_facts: Apply for alien registration immediately when permission to change residency status is granted
Changes of name, passport, school or address are reported within 14 days
reference_answer: When you are granted permission to change your residency status, apply for alien registration immediately. Afterwards, report changes of name, passport details, school, or address within 14 days at an immigration office or online at www.hikorea.go.kr.
notes: Stale profile: visa D-4 updated to D-2 and student_type to degree_seeking; degree_level removed because the history only says "full-time degree program" (9.5).

session_history.text: I was studying Korean at ERICA on D-4 with TOPIK 2.
I entered a degree program this term.

question: My visa is D-2 now. Can I apply for part-time work under the new status?
required_facts: D-2 holders can apply with confirmation from the person in charge, a previous-semester GPA of at least 2.0 and the Korean proficiency requirement
TOPIK Level 2 is below the Level 3 or 4 requirement, so hours are limited to 10 (bachelor) or 15 (master or doctoral)
reference_answer: Yes, you can apply as a D-2 degree student with the OIA confirmation and a previous-semester GPA of at least 2.0. With TOPIK Level 2 you do not meet the Korean requirement (Level 3 for bachelor year 1-2, Level 4 otherwise), so you are limited to 10 hours a week if you are an undergraduate or 15 hours if you are a master or doctoral student, unless you qualify through the English-track test scores.
notes: Stale profile: visa D-4 updated to D-2, student_type degree_seeking, degree_level removed because the new level is not stated (9.5). The degree level decides 10 vs 15 hours (2 branches). GPA for a new entrant is a caveat.

session_history.text: I'm a second-year ERICA undergraduate on D-2.
I have TOPIK level 3 and I'm enrolled full time.

question: How many work hours am I allowed?
required_facts: Bachelor year 1-2 with TOPIK Level 3 may work 30 hours on weekdays
No restriction on weekends and school holidays
reference_answer: As a second-year ERICA undergraduate with TOPIK Level 3 you may work up to 30 hours on weekdays, with no limit on weekends and school holidays, with a part-time permit and a previous-semester GPA of at least 2.0.
notes: All attributes stated in the history; no branch.

session_history.text: I completed my master's coursework at ERICA.
I changed from D-2 to D-10 while looking for a job.

question: Can I do part-time work under that status?
required_facts: D-10 holders may work part time only under the special D-10 provisions
Requirements: changed from D-2-1~4/D-2-7, Korean degree within 3 years, TOPIK Level 4 or higher (or equivalent), no E-1~E-7 experience
reference_answer: Only under the special D-10 provisions: you must have changed from D-2-1~4 or D-2-7 to D-10, hold a Korean degree earned within 3 years, hold TOPIK Level 4 or higher (or the Social Integration Program equivalent), and have no E-1~E-7 work experience. D-10-2 and D-10-3 are excluded.
notes: Same evidence as T14-125. Whether the student already holds a Korean degree is outside the vocabulary (caveat).

session_history.text: I'm an ERICA master's student with all coursework completed.
I'm on D-10 and searching for a job in Korea.

question: Is this career program meant for someone in my situation?
required_facts: The Global Career Start Online Program is open to international graduate students only
It prepares students for employment in Korea
reference_answer: Yes, if you mean the Global Career Start Online Program: it is open to international graduate students only and covers hiring trends, job documents, interviews, and work visa procedures. Its application period (20 October-17 November 2025) has passed.
notes: Referent "this career program" is not in the history (open 10.4.5); I took the ERICA graduate-only career program. Acceptable [answer, clarify].

session_history.text: I'm a non-degree exchange student at ERICA for one term.
I have D-2-8, study in English, and have no TOPIK score.

question: Which insurance applies to me?
required_facts: The university group insurance (KRW 25,000) is billed with tuition
National Health Insurance applies at 50% of an alien resident's monthly premium, billed monthly
reference_answer: At ERICA two insurances apply: the university group insurance (KRW 25,000, added to the tuition bill) and National Health Insurance, charged at 50% of an alien resident's monthly premium with the bill mailed to the address on your Alien Registration Card.
notes: Exchange students may be fee-waived, so whether the group premium appears on a tuition bill is not stated (caveat). Same as the campus branch of T14-132 but campus is fixed by history.

session_history.text: I'm a doctoral student at ERICA and my D-2 is still valid.
I'm graduating soon and want to find a job in Korea.

question: When should I start the D-10 change?
required_facts: Eligibility for the D-10-1 change: legal residence, bachelor degree or higher, points on the job-seeker score table (or an exemption)
When to start the change relative to graduation is not stated
reference_answer: The ERICA Visa page lists who may change from D-2 to D-10-1 (legal residence, bachelor degree or higher, enough job-seeker points, or an exemption) but does not say when to start relative to graduation. Ask the ERICA OIA or the immigration office.
notes: Same as T14-133 (borderline partial vs unanswerable, open 10.4.3).
